name: Saltbone Draw — the Gray Zone Card Game
description: A fully analog trick-taking card game printed on laminated reclaimed-cardboard stock, played in the Gray Zone bars and canteens with no electronic components whatsoever — a deliberate rejection of BCI integration at a time when even playing cards were being fitted with smart-ink. The deck uses the Gray Zone-specific iconography: ration stamps, debt notices, augmentation receipts, and eviction orders serve as suits, while face cards depict anonymized the Gray Zone archetypes rather than corporate royalty. Decks are printed locally in each district, meaning no two Saltbone Draw decks are quite identical.
story_hooks: A rare first-edition deck from 2183 — the original Ashkouri District printing — surfaces in a Mirrorjaw Market stall and multiple parties want it badly enough to cause problems.
A the Gray Zone bar's weekly Saltbone tournament is the cover for a rotating dead-drop network — the game's scoring is a cipher.
Someone has been introducing subtly altered decks into circulation, and the changes in iconography carry a coded political message that only longtime players would notice.
